summary: search_* spliced client filter and sort fields into SQL: an ORDER BY injection and an oracle on hidden columns
detail: Filter and sort column names came from the request and were only quoted, and sort_order went straight into ORDER BY. Filtering or sorting on a hidden column (password_hash) told the caller about values they could not read.
note: 14 Oct 2026: search_* checks filter and sort columns against an allow-list of visible columns built at compile time (PR #8, merged via #11).

summary: Update permission was checked against the request body, so a non-owner could take over any row
detail: save_* evaluated the update rule against p_data. A caller put their own id in the owner field of the body, passed the check, and overwrote someone else's row.
note: 14 Oct 2026: the update rule is evaluated against the stored row (PR #9, merged via #11).

summary: Weak defaults and leaks: JWT secret fell back in production, register_user set any column, expansions and pushes leaked hidden columns
detail: A missing JWT secret fell back to a default in production; register_user accepted arbitrary columns; FK and many-to-many expansion and list subscriptions returned hidden columns; realtime pushes did not re-check access.
note: 14 Oct 2026: JWT secret fails closed in production; register_user column allow-list; expansions and subscriptions project visible columns; pushes re-run can_subscribe and strip hidden columns (PR #10, merged via #11).

summary: Filtered middle hops compiled to FALSE: promoters could do nothing their rules allowed
detail: A middle hop with a filter (->occasion_promoters[occasion_id=$].promoter_id->) was rejected by the parser and the rule compiled to FALSE with only a warning. 31 of modeling-dzql's 204 rules were affected.
note: 14 Oct 2026: every hop compiles to a nested EXISTS, following every matching row. Proved on modeling-dzql's compiled SQL (PR #11).

summary: [org_id=$,role=owner] dropped role=owner, so owner-only rules admitted every member
detail: Only the first pair inside brackets was read. 15 owner-only rules in modeling-dzql were granted to every member.
note: 14 Oct 2026: every condition inside [ ] is read (PR #11).

summary: Create, update and delete enforced only the first rule in a list
detail: Codegen compiled permissions.create[0], update[0] and delete[0]; later rules were ignored.
note: 14 Oct 2026: every rule in a list is enforced; any one grants access (PR #11).

summary: canSubscribe fell back to any signed-in user when a path didn't parse, and canSubscribe: [] meant public
detail: The subscribe compiler was a separate copy: unparseable paths compiled to p_user_id IS NOT NULL, an empty list to RETURN TRUE, list subscriptions ignored their paths, and @field meant acts_for membership.
note: 14 Oct 2026: one compiler for permissions, canSubscribe and notifications. Anything it can't compile is a build error; an empty list denies everyone; TRUE and AUTHENTICATED are explicit (PR #11).

summary: List subscriptions returned every root row, ignoring the entity's view rules
detail: get_<list> returned every row matching root.filter to anyone allowed to subscribe.
note: 14 Oct 2026: the list query applies the root entity's view rules (PR #11).

summary: An editor could move a row to a parent they don't control; key-only entities generated invalid SQL
detail: The update rule was only checked on the stored row, so a promoter could move a package to another org's occasion. An entity with only a key column generated UPDATE t SET WHERE and INSERT INTO t () VALUES ().
note: 14 Oct 2026: the update rule is checked on the stored row and on the row after the change; key-only entities skip the UPDATE and insert DEFAULT VALUES (PR #11).

summary: Realtime pushes for a list reached subscribers who can't view the row
detail: The only push check was can_subscribe, which for a list is a literal, so every change went to every list subscriber.
note: 14 Oct 2026: the runtime calls a generated <name>_can_receive before each push: root rows need the view rules, included rows must be in the subscriber's documents, included deletes go out as their key only (PR #12).

summary: Two dzqls in one repo: the interpreter beside the compiler, and the compiler's folder named tzql
detail: packages/dzql held the deprecated interpreter (dzql-legacy) and packages/tzql the compiler published as dzql, which confused paths, docs and release tags.
note: 14 Oct 2026: interpreter removed, packages/tzql moved to packages/dzql; docs, workflows and test setup follow (PR #13).

summary: Dead duplicate generators, each with a test that tests the dead copy
detail: codegen/pinia.ts (generatePiniaStore) is never used: the CLI uses subscribable_store.ts. codegen/realtime.ts (generateAffectedKeysFunction) is never used: the compiler uses the one in subscribable_sql.ts. tests/pinia.test.ts and tests/realtime.test.ts test the dead copies, a false green. Remove both modules; move any assertion worth keeping onto the live generators.

summary: Unused functions and arguments
detail: stripReferences, formatValidationResults and validatePath are defined and never called. compilePermission's context argument is unused at every call site.

summary: A build artifact and old notes are committed
detail: tsconfig.tsbuildinfo changes on every tsc run; untrack it and add it to .gitignore. docs/feature-requests/ is closed bug reports and a stale gap list; docs/futures.md is ideas, now items in this file. Remove both.

summary: Temporal entities get parallel copies of save and delete
detail: generateTemporalSaveFunction and generateTemporalDeleteFunction repeat most of the normal generators, so every fix has to be made twice (the October permission fixes were). Fold them into one generator with temporal branches; the temporal integration tests are the safety net. Keep the feature.

summary: Affected keys are found by guessing foreign-key names
detail: generateAffectedKeysFunction derives FK columns from relation names (rel + _id) and a singularize that strips a trailing s. Use the includes' declared filters and the schema's REFERENCES instead, and fail the build when a relation can't be resolved.

summary: Whether a rule reads JSONB or a row is decided by the variable's name
detail: toSource treats any name starting p_ or v_ as JSONB. Callers should pass a RowSource explicitly; most already can.

summary: The logger is 300 lines
detail: Check what of it is used and shrink it to that.

summary: Generated functions are SECURITY DEFINER, so the generated predicate is the only guard
detail: Any compiler bug in a permission check is a data leak, as October showed. The handover's direction for delta: run compiled functions as the invoker under FORCE RLS so row-level security is the backstop. Decide whether dzql adopts that or the path compiler moves to delta.

summary: Included rows in a subscription are not filtered by their own entities' view rules
detail: A document shows every included row of a root the subscriber may see. Documented in for_ai.md; decide whether includes should apply their own view rules.

summary: The October changes are unreleased and include breaking changes
detail: Empty rule lists now deny, paths that can't compile fail the build, @field in canSubscribe changed, updates are checked on the new row. Release as 0.7.0, with CHANGELOG Unreleased becoming 0.7.0. Before tagging: the create-dzql end-to-end Playwright check from CLAUDE.md.

summary: CI is disabled
detail: ci.yml runs only on manual dispatch ('needs fixes for Bun download issues'), and it runs bun test without the Docker database the suite expects. Fix it so the suite runs on every push and pull request.
note: 2026-10-15: ci.yml runs on every push to main and pull request, Bun pinned at 1.4.3 (setup-bun@v2), the Postgres service as the database, tsc then bun test.

summary: Large documents are built as one JSON value
detail: From docs/futures.md: a subscribable document is assembled in memory as one jsonb. Measure with large lists; consider streaming or paging.

summary: Notifications are computed inside the write transaction
detail: From docs/futures.md: affected keys and notify users are computed per write. Consider decoupling, logical replication (WAL) instead of LISTEN/NOTIFY, and a prepared statement cache. can_receive now adds a query per subscriber per push; measure it.
